instruction: Change the display name of the email account "anonym-x2024@outlook.com" to "Work Email".

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the account display name from 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com' to 'Work Email' in Thunderbird. The evaluator first identifies which server (server1, server2, etc.) is associated with the email account 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com' by checking mail.server.serverN.userName preferences, then verifies that the corresponding mail.server.serverN.name is set to 'Work Email'. This is verified by reading the prefs.js file from the Thunderbird profile.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction by dynamically identifying which server is associated with 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com' and checking its display name.

Metric uses a robust two-pass approach: (1) searches all mail.server.serverN.userName preferences to find the server with the target email, (2) verifies that server's name preference equals 'Work Email'.
Logic correctly handles multiple email accounts - does NOT hardcode server1, contrary to previous judgment.
Complete coverage: verifies the exact requirement in the instruction (changing display name of specific email account).
Handles edge cases appropriately (server not found, preference not found, file read errors).
Minor concern: No postconfig to ensure Thunderbird saves prefs.js to disk, but Thunderbird typically auto-saves preferences so this is unlikely to cause issues in practice.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a postconfig step to ensure Thunderbird has flushed preferences to disk (e.g., close account settings dialog or add a brief delay), though this is a minor optimization rather than a critical fix.
